A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same constrained reinforcement-learning work for quantum control. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations of population transfer, Rydberg gates, and transmon reset, including fidelity, robustness, ablation, and computational timing results.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation results and adds algorithm comparisons, runtime measurements, and analyses of learned control signals. These are simulation results, not new physical-device experiments.

M1.justification: The constrained PPO framework, filtering, endpoint constraints, and multi-step feedback procedure remain. However, the stated low-pass smoothness penalty changes from an integrated signed residual in v1 Eq. E4 to an integrated absolute residual in v2 Eq. 23, altering the documented reward component. The PDFs do not establish whether this also changed the implementation.

E1.justification: The three quantum platforms and their control tasks remain. Noise-test coverage expands modestly: v2 Fig. 9 includes a Λ-system amplitude-noise level of 3 MHz alongside the 0.1 and 1 MHz levels shown in v1 Fig. 7. The new hardware-feasibility discussion does not introduce a physical-device study.

E2.justification: V2 adds Krotov to the Λ-system comparison and evaluates vanilla PPO plus constrained and vanilla DDPG/TD3 variants in the Λ and two-photon Rydberg environments. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set beyond v1. The retained 0.83 entry is relabeled PINN, rather than representing an additional baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces controlled RL comparisons with common batches and update budgets, CPU convergence-time benchmarking, and a 1 GSa/s waveform-analysis protocol. The reported Λ-system BFGS iteration limit also changes from 10,000 in v1 Table II to 1,000 in v2 Table 1 despite an unchanged score; this does not establish that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds constrained-versus-vanilla algorithm ablations in Figs. 2 and 12, an RL-versus-optimal-control state-evolution comparison in Fig. 10, and smoothing-dependent waveform analysis in Fig. 15. It revises the Λ noise study and omits v1 Fig. 10's quantitative single-photon Rydberg noise analysis. Existing pulse-area and smoothing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The main comparison table retains its 32-seed reporting. New Fig. 2 explicitly reports two seeds and one-standard-deviation shading. For Λ noise robustness, v1 Fig. 7 reports min/max envelopes, whereas v2 Fig. 9 reports standard-deviation envelopes. These are reporting changes, not evidence of increased replication for existing results.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial numerical comparison and timing results, including Krotov fidelity 0.99 ± 0.001 and CPU convergence times of 239.1 seconds for PPO versus 3997 seconds for Krotov. The reported 0.25-microsecond Rydberg pulse fidelity changes from 0.9993 to 0.99958 alongside a revised waveform. Noise curves and the transmon solver-step curve also change; the principal Λ and transmon headline fidelities remain.

T1.justification: The absolute-value addition changes the mathematical smoothness definition, and v2 Fig. 15 introduces a sampled-waveform diagnostic. Most quantum and PPO equations are retained or relocated, without new proofs. The printed single-photon Hamiltonian summation limit also changes from 2 to 1 in Eq. 14 without explanation.

C1.justification: The central claims of efficient constrained RL, fidelities above 0.999 across three systems, and noise robustness remain. V2 explicitly quantifies the Λ-system advantage as almost two orders of magnitude lower infidelity and extends the conclusion's applicability claim to noisy physical control more generally.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops practical applicability through measurement-budget estimates in Appendix F and hardware-bandwidth interpretations in Fig. 15. Appendix G.3 attributes much of the runtime advantage to compilation and automatic differentiation, qualifying the role of constraints. The conclusion adds error-correction relevance and cross-device policy generalization, while retaining the principal modelling and non-adiabatic limitations.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code and data release; v2 states that code is open source and supplies a repository address. V2 also adds a detailed PPO/DDPG/TD3 hyperparameter table, CleanRL implementation information, and hardware, batching, and timing details. These materially expand reproducibility documentation; repository contents were not independently checked.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against Krotov, hybrid optimal control, logical-level quantum RL, error correction, compilation, and recent transmon-control work. It revises the discussion of model-based RL and replaces v1's categorical RL-versus-direct-differentiation table with more contextual comparisons. These changes extend beyond bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method explanation undergo substantial rewriting. Quantum-control background moves from the main text to Appendix B, implementation material is reorganized into Appendix G, and experimental-feasibility and impact sections are added. Terminology and section conventions are revised throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ICML layout, expands and restructures the main comparison table, adds hyperparameter and timing tables, and introduces several analytical figures. V1's two-panel multi-step figure is redrawn as a combined main-text plot; noise and Rydberg plots are revised. The conceptual comparison table and single-photon noise plot are removed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central constrained-RL claim through vanilla-versus-constrained comparisons and broader baselines, addressing important gaps in v1. Hyperparameter disclosure, runtime benchmarks, and the code-access statement also materially improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed single-photon robustness evidence and localized equation/reporting inconsistencies. Physical-device feasibility remains an extrapolation rather than experimentally validated evidence.
